icml2025-0008-position-algebra-unveils-d.after: \[\begin{aligned}\Pr(|\overline Z|\ge\tfrac12)&=\frac{2\sum_{k=0}^{5}\binom{20}{k}}{2^{20}}=\frac{43400}{1048576}\approx0.0413894653,\\2e^{-20(1/2)^2}&=2e^{-5}\approx0.0134758940.\end{aligned}\] The actual probability exceeds the asserted upper bound: 43400/1048576 equals 5425/131072 exactly. The existing finite enumeration is not a simulation or an asymptotic approximation. A charitable interpretation that restricts B.1 to nonnegative losses excludes this example, but adds a hypothesis absent from its literal statement. The earlier conditional positive-definite-loss discussion on p.13 identifies the interpolation set with the zero empirical-loss locus; it does not state that condition as a hypothesis of B.1. This finding does not establish failure for every conventional squared-loss application, nor does excluding this example by a new assumption alone validate the published exponent.

The paper explicitly discloses test-set best-of-\(N\) selection on p. 4, which limits the criticism, but does not explain the additional fit/evaluation reuse or different targets. Exact historical masks, model identifiers, and run provenance are needed before assigning these released discrepancies to every published accuracy curve. README Guard-model commands and the manuscript’s Instruct-model setup also require reconciliation.
